concerns.text: Task T000aa hardcodes citations with '[UNRESOLVED-CLAIM]' status markers as input arguments. This violates Constitution Principle II (Verified Accuracy) which mandates that citations MUST be verified before contributing to the project. A task cannot begin by assuming unverified claims; the input must be the raw citation string, and the verification logic must determine validity, not pre-assert failure.

Task T007e requires creating 'docs/trust_scale_items.md' containing the 'verbatim 12-item Lee & See (2004) [UNRESOLVED-CLAIM...]' scale. This task attempts to implement a core measurement instrument (FR-002, SC-004) while explicitly acknowledging the source citation is unverified. This is a semantic weakening of the 'Verified Accuracy' constraint; the task must be gated behind successful citation validation (T000c) and cannot proceed with an unverified source.

Task T016 requires reading verbatim trust items from 'docs/trust_scale_items.md' at runtime. However, the task description includes the citation 'Lee & See (2004) [UNRESOLVED-CLAIM...]' within the task text itself, implying the task is defined around an unverified source. This creates a circular dependency where the implementation relies on a document that cannot be legally created until the citation is verified, yet the task list treats the unverified state as a valid starting point.

Phase 0 tasks (T000aa-T000ad) define a 'citation validation script' that takes pre-marked 'UNRESOLVED-CLAIM' strings as input. This reverses the constitutional flow: the system should accept raw citations, validate them, and *then* flag failures. By baking the 'unresolved' status into the task input, the task list presumes the failure of the verification process before it runs, violating the 'Verified Accuracy' gate logic.
